content.user_title: Master Prompt and Context Engineering Standards
content.value_statement: Writing prompts for AI agents without a consistent standard leads to bloated, low-signal context that degrades model performance. This skill gives your agents clear, Anthropic-aligned rules for structure, clarity, and just-in-time context loading.
actual_capabilities: Provides a documented standard for structuring prompts into Background, Instructions, Examples, and Constraints sections.
Explains context engineering principles such as finite attention budget and signal-to-noise optimization.
Offers reusable Markdown templates for basic context, agent-specific context, and command documentation.
Includes best-practice and anti-pattern checklists for reviewing prompt and context files.
Describes context management strategies including just-in-time loading, compaction, note-taking, and sub-agent architectures.
Supplies a create-prompt and optimize-prompt workflow to guide authoring and refinement.
limitations: This is documentation and guidance only; it does not run code or automate prompt changes.
The standards are opinionated and based on one set of best practices; they may not fit every model or use case.
It does not measure prompt performance or provide evaluation tooling.
It assumes familiarity with Markdown and general AI agent concepts.

use_cases.title: Standardize a team prompt library
use_cases.description: A platform team adopts these standards to keep every agent prompt structured, minimal, and consistent across projects.

use_cases.title: Review and improve an existing prompt
use_cases.description: A developer applies the anti-pattern checklist to trim verbose instructions and raise the signal-to-noise ratio of a prompt.

use_cases.title: Design context for a new agent
use_cases.description: A prompt author uses the agent-specific template to define role, capabilities, tools, and constraints for a new agent.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a simple prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the prompting standards, help me write a clear prompt for an agent that summarizes customer support tickets. Include Background, Instructions, and Constraints sections.

prompt_templates.title: Trim a verbose prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt and rewrite it to follow the signal-to-noise standards. Remove verbose explanations and vague words like might and could. Prompt: [paste prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Build an agent context file
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an agent-specific context file for a code review agent using the standard template. Define its role, capabilities, available tools, workflow, and constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Apply just-in-time context loading
prompt_templates.prompt: My agent prompt includes a full product catalog inline. Refactor it to use just-in-time context loading with lightweight identifiers and a retrieval reference, following the context management strategies.

output_examples.input: Help me structure a prompt for a tax calculation agent.
output_examples.output: The skill guides you to split the prompt into Background Information, Instructions in imperative voice, concrete Examples, and clear Constraints. It suggests referencing a tax tool by name and parameters rather than embedding raw tax data, keeping the context minimal and high-signal.

output_examples.input: My prompt is too long and the agent misses instructions.
output_examples.output: The skill points to the anti-pattern checklist: remove verbose explanations, cut redundant sections, and replace inline data dumps with just-in-time references. It recommends measuring performance, pruning low-value tokens, and iterating on the result.

best_practices: Organize every prompt into clear Markdown sections and use imperative, specific instructions.
Load detailed data just-in-time with lightweight identifiers instead of embedding large inline dumps.
Prune redundant and low-value content regularly to protect the model's limited attention budget.
anti_patterns: Writing verbose, hedge-filled instructions that use words like might, could, or should consider.
Dumping full datasets or historical context into the prompt before it is actually needed.
Defining overlapping tools or unstructured paragraphs where a focused list would be clearer.

faq.question: What does this skill actually do?
faq.answer: It provides a written standard and templates for engineering prompts and context for AI agents. It is guidance, not an automation tool.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex, and its principles apply to most large language model prompts.

faq.question: Does this skill run any code or scripts?
faq.answer: No. It contains only Markdown documentation. There are no scripts, network calls, or file system operations.

faq.question: Is it based on any official guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It is based on Anthropic's article on effective context engineering for AI agents.

faq.question: Who benefits most from this skill?
faq.answer: Prompt engineers, application developers, and AI platform teams who want consistent, high-quality prompt and context files.

faq.question: Can I use the templates directly?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes basic context, agent-specific, and command templates that you can copy and fill in for your own agents.
